newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Portugal rejects EU demand to end EPAC grain aid.
newsitem.headline: Portugal rejects EU demand to end EPAC grain aid.

text.p: Portugal has rejected a request by the European Commission to stop granting official aid to publicly owned cereals marketing company Empresa para a Agroalimentacao e Cereais SA (EPAC), EU sources said.
"The response was negative," said a source.
The Commission's request was made in a letter to the Portuguese government on April 30 asking for a response by mid-May.
"The Portuguese replied on May 22 and the Commission is studying the response," said a Commission official, declining to give further details.
The Portuguse government is considering turning EPAC into a private company but would first have to help it clear its substantial debts which would conflict with EU state aid rules.
In February, the Commission opened an inquiry into 154 million Ecus of state aid granted to EPAC.

Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby, said it wrote last week to EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to complain that EPAC had been granted the entire 150,000 tonnes reduced tariff quota for maize imports into Portugal.
"EPAC's bid was much lower because it receives state aid," a Coceral official said.
